verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and none is at level 1: the problem is stated and the demand objection was refuted. The four surviving objections are fixable level 2 points. standards-compat-2 and maintenance-fit-2 need someone who has the standard text and knows the SQL/JSON node design. maintenance-fit-1 and standards-compat-1 are design points the author can answer on the list.

brief.title: Add SQL-standard JSON_TRANSFORM for declarative jsonb modification
brief.problem: Postgres has only its own jsonb_set, jsonb_insert and jsonb_delete_path for changing a JSON value, with no SQL-standard spelling. Those functions cannot act on every member at one level in one call, have no "replace, else error" or "insert unless present" rules, and return NULL when the new value is NULL. The author writes for users who want portable, declarative JSON mutation.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds JSON_TRANSFORM (SQL/JSON T883, subclause 6.44) as a JsonExpr op that applies one INSERT, REPLACE, REMOVE or RENAME at a jsonpath target. The executor rebuilds the input jsonb in one streaming pass instead of calling jsonb_set and its siblings. Per-operation ON EXISTING, ON MISSING, ON NULL, ON EMPTY and ON ERROR clauses, lax/strict target paths and a "= PATH <jsonpath>" source are also supported.
user_visible_surface: New SQL syntax: JSON_TRANSFORM(doc, INSERT | REPLACE | REMOVE | RENAME path [= value | = PATH jsonpath] [behaviors]), returning jsonb.
New behavior clauses per operation: ON EXISTING, ON MISSING, ON NULL, ON EMPTY, ON ERROR, with standard implicit defaults.
Two new unreserved keywords, EXISTING and MISSING; IGNORE gets a grammar precedence to share use with IGNORE NULLS.
Wildcard '.*' allowed in target paths; REMOVE and REPLACE may end in it, INSERT and RENAME may not.
Deparse output for JSON_TRANSFORM in EXPLAIN VERBOSE and stored expressions such as index definitions.
author_claims: It is the SQL-standard, portable form of JSON mutation, where the jsonb_* functions are Postgres-specific.
One call can do what the jsonb_* functions cannot, such as REMOVE '$.*.password' or conditional insert and replace.
The streaming pass is O(size) however many members an action touches, against O(N * size) by delegation.
INSERT, RENAME and empty-wildcard behavior match both the standard and Oracle; lax/strict handling matches jsonb_path_query().
Peter Eisentraut suggested the feature and guided the author off-list.
brief.thread_state: Zsolt Parragi reviewed v1 and v2 against Oracle docs, found crashes, missing deparse and lax-mode gaps, all addressed by v4 (five patches). No one has answered whether to stay with the standard's single operation per call or allow Oracle-style multiple operations, and the listed reviewer has not posted.
unclear: Nobody in the thread has checked the patch against the standard text; the only reviewer used Oracle documentation.
The material shows no documentation hunks or regression test files, so user docs and test coverage are unknown.
The proposal does not say whether JSON_TRANSFORM accepts json input or only jsonb, or whether a RETURNING clause exists.
Array position targets (e.g. '$.arr[0]') and filter expressions in target paths are not addressed.
RENAME collisions reuse the generic duplicate-key error, and the proposal does not say if a specific error is planned.
The thread does not show performance numbers comparing JSON_TRANSFORM with jsonb_set.

prior_attempts.title: Add jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to)
prior_attempts.who_objected: Andrew Dunstan, Pavel Stehule, Peter Eisentraut
prior_attempts.quote: Blindly replacing every instance of a single string regardless of context seems at best a niche use. Is there any reason not to make this an extension?
prior_attempts.reason: Andrew Dunstan judged blind replacement of every instance of a string, regardless of context, to be a niche use and asked why it could not be an extension. Pavel Stehule suggested using JsonPath to say what to replace, and Peter Eisentraut pointed to json_transform in Oracle and the SQL standard draft, noting that json_transform and json_translate together might confuse users. The thread ends there, and the author later withdrew the entry.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 replaced every value that equals a given string, with no context. This proposal targets values by jsonpath with SQL-standard syntax, which replies in P1 pointed to as the alternative.

objections.title: Claimed portability rests on a subset of T883 nobody checked against the text
objections.failure_scenario: A user ports a query that uses an array position target such as '$.arr[0]', a filter, a RETURNING clause or a json input. It fails or returns jsonb with a changed key order. If Postgres later corrects a default to match the standard text, views and indexes created earlier behave differently after upgrade.
objections.argument: Portability is the main argument in message #1. The proposal does not cover array positions, filters, RETURNING or json input, although the existing JSON_QUERY and JSON_VALUE support RETURNING. The only reviewer used Oracle documentation without the standard (messages #2, #5), so defaults such as ERROR ON MISSING for an empty wildcard rest only on the author's reading (message #3). Deparse writes the defaults explicitly, which helps dumps, but a stored behavior that was wrong would still need a compatibility break to fix.
objections.author_must_show: Which parts of T883 does the patch cover, which parts are left out, and has someone with the standard text confirmed the chosen defaults?

critic.reasoning: The 0002 walker handles only key and wildcard steps, and the only reviewer says in messages #2 and #5 that he cannot check the standard. RETURNING and json input are unstated, not shown absent, so that part should be put as a question.

objections.title: Reusing JsonExpr with a NULL path_spec breaks existing walkers
objections.failure_scenario: Code in core or an extension that handles JsonExpr assumes path_spec is set, as contain_mutable_functions_walker did. A JSON_TRANSFORM expression reaches it and the backend crashes. This happens at run time, in a path nobody tested, such as CREATE INDEX in message #5.
objections.argument: JSON_TRANSFORM is added as a JsonExpr op whose jsonpath lives in a new action field, while path_spec stays NULL. Review already found three crashes from this, in the expression walker, the mutator and clauses.c (messages #4 and #6), and each fix was a local special case. Every future consumer of JsonExpr has to remember the same special case, and nothing enforces it.
objections.author_must_show: Why is JSON_TRANSFORM a JsonExpr op and not its own node, and how are all JsonExpr consumers in core shown to handle a NULL path_spec?

critic.reasoning: One correction: only the clauses.c crash came from the NULL path_spec; message #4 traces the walker and mutator crashes to the untraversed action field. The concern stands, because the thread does not say why JSON_TRANSFORM reuses JsonExpr or how other consumers were checked.

objections.title: Second jsonpath walker duplicates jsonpath_exec semantics in the executor
objections.failure_scenario: A later release extends jsonpath, for example with a new accessor or changed lax unwrapping rules, and updates jsonpath_exec.c. The JSON_TRANSFORM walker in execExprInterp.c keeps the old behaviour without any error. Users then see JSON_TRANSFORM and jsonb_path_query() disagree on the same path, and find out from a bug report.
objections.argument: Patch 0002 adds its own path-to-steps converter and recursive rebuilder (jtSetPath, jtSetPathObject). Patch 0004 then adds lax/strict handling "similar to jsonb_path_query" as separate code. The walker accepts only key and wildcard steps, so array positions and filters, listed as open in the brief, would need a third copy of path logic. Nothing shown makes the two evaluators share code or tests that would fail when they diverge.
objections.author_must_show: Can the target-path matching reuse jsonpath_exec.c, or which shared tests fail when JSON_TRANSFORM and jsonb_path_query() disagree on a path?

critic.reasoning: The 0002 commit message describes a self-contained path-to-steps converter and walker, and 0004 adds lax/strict handling to it separately. The material names no shared code or test that fails when it and jsonb_path_query() disagree.

objections.title: IGNORE ON clause may not parse after a function-call value
objections.failure_scenario: A user writes `json_transform(j, replace '$.a' = to_jsonb(x) ignore on missing)`. The value ends in a function call, so the parser may treat IGNORE as the start of IGNORE NULLS and then fail on ON. The user gets a syntax error for a form the standard allows.
objections.argument: Patch 0003 resolves the IGNORE NULLS / IGNORE ON conflict by giving IGNORE_P a precedence that always shifts toward IGNORE NULLS after a function application. That keeps window syntax working, but it seems to send exactly the case where a value or PATH source ends in a function call down the wrong branch. The commit message does not say whether that case parses, and nothing in the thread tests it. Silencing a grammar conflict with precedence hides it from future gram.y changes.
objections.author_must_show: Does `replace '$.a' = some_func(x) ignore on missing` parse, and if so, which grammar rule makes it work despite the IGNORE_P precedence?

critic.reasoning: The 0003 commit message says the parser shifts IGNORE toward NULLS after a function application, and no example in the thread has a function-call value followed by IGNORE ON. The grammar is not shown, so the material cannot rule out the syntax error.

refuted.title: Expression indexes freeze semantics that no one has checked against the standard
refuted.failure_scenario: A user builds an expression index or a stored generated column on JSON_TRANSFORM(j, REMOVE 'lax $.*.k') in release 20. Release 21 fixes the behavior after someone checks the standard. pg_upgrade keeps the old index files, so index scans and heap rechecks disagree and queries silently return wrong rows until someone runs REINDEX.
refuted.argument: Message #5 and message #6 show JSON_TRANSFORM is accepted in index expressions and treated as immutable. The only review used Oracle documentation (message #2, message #5). The author made several semantic calls from his own reading of the standard: the INSERT no-op on a missing parent, the empty wildcard counting as missing, and lax unwrapping (message #3, message #6). Any later fix to these changes stored results that pg_upgrade carries over unchanged.
refuted.author_must_show: Before the first release that allows JSON_TRANSFORM in indexes, will someone with the standard text confirm the semantics of empty-match, lax-unwrap and missing-parent?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which already covers the unchecked semantics and their effect on stored indexes. The pg_upgrade consequence applies to a behavior fix in any new immutable function, and Postgres handles such fixes with a release-note REINDEX instruction.

refuted.title: No committer has engaged on a large new SQL/JSON surface
refuted.failure_scenario: The patch is committed with semantics checked only against Oracle documentation. Later someone with the standard text finds a deviation in a default behaviour that index definitions and views already store. Changing it then breaks existing users, and keeping it means defending a non-standard default for good.
refuted.argument: The patch adds grammar, keywords, a JsonExpr op, JIT support, deparse and a separate document rebuilder. The only public reviewer said he cannot check the standard (messages #2 and #5). Peter Eisentraut's guidance was off-list, and the listed reviewer has not posted. The single-operation versus multiple-operation question from messages #1 and #3 is still open, and the answer fixes the node and the deparse format.
refuted.author_must_show: Which committer with access to SQL:2023 will review the semantics and the single-operation versus multiple-operation choice before it is fixed in stored deparse output?

critic.reasoning: The failure scenario is a duplicate of standards-compat-2. The rest is a committability note, which the rubric keeps apart from the verdict, and message #1 gives a path from one operation to a list that keeps single-operation deparse output valid.

refuted.title: Portability benefit not shown for the single-operation form
refuted.failure_scenario: A user moves an Oracle query such as JSON_TRANSFORM(doc, REMOVE '$.a', SET '$.b' = 1) to Postgres. It fails at parse time because the patch accepts one operation per call. The user then rewrites it as nested calls or with jsonb_set, and portability gives that user nothing.
refuted.argument: The material gives two sources of demand: the SQL standard and Peter Eisentraut's suggestion in the jsonb_translate thread [P1]. No field report or -general request appears, and no reviewer in messages #2 and #5 asks for the feature. The main claim is portability, but the only other implementation cited is Oracle, and message #1 says Oracle's form takes a list of operations. The question in messages #1 and #3 of whether to follow the standard's single operation or Oracle's list has had no answer, so the main claimed benefit does not yet have a defined target.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users or migrations need JSON_TRANSFORM, and do they use the single-operation form that the standard defines or Oracle's operation lists?

critic.reasoning: The material shows demand evidence the rubric accepts: a SQL-standard feature (T883), an Oracle implementation, and a committer's on-list suggestion recorded in P1. Message #1 also names cases jsonb_set cannot do in one call; the Oracle list form is an open scope question.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: JSON_TRANSFORM is accepted in expression indexes, so a later change to its semantics affects index contents kept by pg_upgrade.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: Stored expressions in views, indexes and defaults carry the new JsonExpr op and its action fields.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes JsonExpr in primnodes.h and adds parse nodes, which extensions that walk expression trees see.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch adds JSON_TRANSFORM syntax, the keywords EXISTING and MISSING, and a precedence for IGNORE.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: Patches 0004 and 0005 change clauses.c, including the mutability check for the new op.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: The new ruleutils deparse must reproduce every operation and behavior clause for stored expressions.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a separate jsonpath target walker in execExprInterp.c, JIT support, grammar and deparse code.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which parts of T883 does the patch cover, which does it leave out, and has someone with the standard text confirmed the chosen defaults?
Does JSON_TRANSFORM accept json input or a RETURNING clause, and are array position targets such as '$.arr[0]' and filter expressions rejected with an error?
Why is JSON_TRANSFORM a JsonExpr op with a NULL path_spec instead of its own node, and how were the other JsonExpr consumers in core checked?
Can target-path matching reuse jsonpath_exec.c, or which shared tests fail when JSON_TRANSFORM and jsonb_path_query() disagree on a path?
Does `replace '$.a' = some_func(x) ignore on missing` parse, and which grammar rule makes it work despite the IGNORE_P precedence?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the SQL/JSON grammar and JsonExpr execution and who has the SQL standard text. Message #1 reports off-list guidance from Peter Eisentraut, but the visible messages show no committer posting.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the semantics of each operation and default once views and expression indexes store them, and for a second jsonpath walker that must follow jsonpath_exec.c in every later release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered review within a day in message #3 and posted four versions that address the reported crashes and gaps.

priority.reason: Five patches touch the grammar, parse analysis, the executor, JIT, clauses.c and ruleutils, and the semantics need a check against the standard that the only reviewer could not do. The goal has a standard feature and an on-list suggestion behind it, but no committer has posted in the visible thread.

provisional_note: Only 3 of 8 messages and no code, documentation or tests were read. The grammar behavior for IGNORE after a function call, the json input and RETURNING support, and the handling of unsupported path steps could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Jsonb transform for pl/python
precedents_retrieved.summary: A set of extensions (jsonb_plpythonu, jsonb_plpython2u, jsonb_plpython3u) implementing a CREATE TRANSFORM for jsonb in PL/Python, mapping jsonb objects to dicts, arrays to lists, and numerics to Python Decimal via string conversion, and back. The transform works in both directions so functions can take and return jsonb as native Python values.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The reviewer objected that the third version turned unsupported Python objects such as set() into JSON strings instead of raising an error, asked for tests and errors for complex numbers and ranges, and reported that the tests failed on Python 3. The author sent no revised version after that review, and the commitfest manager returned the patch with feedback because it still needed work and had had no updates for more than a week.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So this still needs more work.. I am marking it as returned with
feedback as there has been no updates for more than 1 week.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize JsonbContainerTypeName by reordering type checks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reorders the checks in JsonbContainerTypeName() so that the array and object bit checks run before the scalar check. The author argued that this avoids calling JsonbExtractScalar() in most cases and reported about 0.8% higher tps for jsonb_typeof().
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley argued that one function call cannot change the speed of a whole query by a measurable amount. His test called the function 1 million times and found the patch 3.5% slower, and perf top showed JsonbExtractScalar using little CPU time. Andreas Karlsson added that scalars are not clearly less common, so the new order would slow some workloads while it speeds up others.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It'll amount to a few dozen instructions for the function out of several 10s of millions, when you consider the cost of processing the entire query.

precedents_retrieved.title: jsonb array-style subscription
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add array-style subscripting to jsonb, so that values can be read with expressions like test_json['a']['a1'] and updated with assignments like UPDATE ... SET test_json['a']['a1']['a2'] = 42. The work-in-progress patch did this by extending the existing ArrayRef node, using the parser's hard-coded array subscript handling, to cover jsonb.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The early messages raise design concerns: using array syntax as key/value syntax, update assignments creating missing intermediate objects, and the lack of an operator that could use a GIN index. The visible messages end in August 2015 and the decision was in March 2016, so the shown text does not connect any of these concerns to the outcome.

precedents_retrieved.title: Collecting statistics about contents of JSONB columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a jsonb_typanalyze function that extracts every path from sampled JSONB documents and stores per-path statistics as an array of JSONB documents in pg_statistic under a new stakind. It also adds an "oprstat" procedure for operators such as ->> so the planner can derive statistics for expressions on JSONB columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tests showed ANALYZE becoming much slower: about 28 seconds against 120 ms on one data set, and over 2 hours or OOM on documents with about 850k distinct paths, because the patch loops over all sample rows once per path. The reviewers agreed the design of collecting statistics for every path in every JSONB column needs rethinking, for example by keeping only the most common paths or enabling the statistics per column. Nikita Glukhov posted optimizations and planned common-path collection, but in the last week of the commitfest the patch no longer applied and Greg Stark asked for a rebase.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: From these points, we can say that we should rethink our design to collect stats for all paths.

precedents_retrieved.title: Storage layer hooks to enable data transformation in extensions
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Storage layer hooks to enable data transformation in extensions
Threads: RFC: PostgreSQL Storage I/O Transformation Hooks

roaster_notes.note: No precedent rejection applies. P1 died as a niche, context-free operation that could live in an extension, and this proposal answers that with jsonpath targets and standard syntax. P4 and P6 share only the jsonb or SQL/JSON area and record no reason that applies here.

The single-operation form can grow into a comma-separated list later without breaking existing calls, so the open direction question is not a compatibility objection. The keywords are unreserved, and deparse writes explicit behaviors, which helps the pg_dump round-trip.
There is no new WAL, on-disk or wire-protocol state. The only persistent state is stored expressions such as views, indexes and defaults, which pg_dump handles through the new ruleutils deparse.

JSON_TRANSFORM is a pure function of its jsonb input and needs no new privilege, file access or cross-session state, so this angle finds no privilege or exposure issue. Without the code, two things cannot be checked: that a JSON_TRANSFORM node is treated as leaky in security barrier views and RLS quals, and that the RENAME duplicate-key error reveals no more than existing jsonb errors do.
There is no hot-path cost for non-users. The cost falls on users of the feature and on future maintainers.

Existing tools cover only part of this. jsonb_set, jsonb_insert, the #- operator and jsonb_set_lax (for NULL handling) cover single-path edits. No core function or extension removes or replaces every member matched by '.*' in one call, and standard grammar such as JSON_TRANSFORM can only live in core. Postgres already added JSON_QUERY and JSON_VALUE next to the jsonb_path_* functions, so adding a standard spelling beside a native one follows existing practice.
Standard conformance and a committer's suggestion are real but modest signals. The only objection asks for evidence of demand and for an answer to the single-operation versus Oracle-style question.
